Convert identifiers between formats

Source: R/convert.R
id_convert.Rd

id_convert() moves values between formats that hold the same bits: "uuid", "ulid", "typeid" and "upid" (128 bits), and "xid" and "objectid" (96 bits, laid out alike). The bytes are kept and the text is rewritten.

Usage

id_convert(x, to, prefix = NULL)

Arguments

x

A zuid vector.

to

The format to convert to.

prefix

For to = "typeid", the prefix of every value, "" for none. NULL keeps the prefixes of a TypeID and means "" otherwise.

Value

A zuid vector of format to.

Details

  • A UUID becomes a TypeID under prefix, and a TypeID becomes a UUID by dropping it.

  • A UPID becomes a UUID as the reference converts it, keeping the bits.

  • A ULID and a UUID convert by reinterpreting the bits. id_fields() then reports what the bits say: most ULIDs read as UUIDs of the "future" variant, and a UUID read as a ULID has its first 48 bits as a time, which is meaningful for version 7 only.

Any other pair is a zuid_convert_error: the target would need a value the source does not have. To change a UUID's text form, use id_format().

Examples

x <- id_parse("01890a5d-ac96-774b-bcce-b302099a8057", "uuid")
t <- id_convert(x, "typeid", prefix = "user")
t
#> <zuid_typeid[1]>
#> [1] user_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q
id_convert(t, "uuid")
#> <zuid_uuid[1]>
#> [1] 01890a5d-ac96-774b-bcce-b302099a8057
id_convert(x, "ulid")
#> <zuid_ulid[1]>
#> [1] 01H455VB4PEX5VSKNK084SN02Q
